title: Check yourself: what a record declares for you

questions.stem: Given `record Point(int x, int y) {}` and a variable `p` holding one, how does code in another class read the first coordinate?

options.says: A record's accessor is named after its component, with no get prefix, so no getX() method exists.
The page shows p.x(), 'Not p.getX()': the accessor has the component's own name.
The component fields are implicitly private, so another class cannot read the field directly.

questions.stem: Which of these lines, placed in the body of `record Counter(String name) { ... }`, fails to compile?

options.says: A record may declare static fields; only instance fields outside the header are refused.
A record body may declare its own instance methods.
A record cannot declare an instance field outside its header: the compiler says 'field declaration must be static'.
